subjects.name: The would-be assassins of Benito Mussolini

summary: Margaret Killjoy recounts the anarchists, socialists and others, among them Violet Gibson, Gino Lucetti and Anteo Zamboni, who tried to assassinate Benito Mussolini in Fascist Italy between 1925 and 1932.
keywords: Cool People Who Did Cool Stuff

evidence.note: 1898 Italian food riots and massacre that motivated Bresci
Bresci kills King Umberto I in July 1900, the only successful assassin covered
Zaniboni's 1925 rifle plot after the Matteotti murder, foiled by an informant
Violet Gibson, Dublin-born, shoots Mussolini in Rome in April 1926; long segment
Western press, notably the New York Times, praising Mussolini; recurs through the story
Sacco and Vanzetti case in the US and Mussolini's use of it
Lucetti throws a grenade at Mussolini's car in Rome; later prison years
Gino Bibbi fights in the Spanish Civil War, later joins Italian partisans
Anteo Zamboni, Bologna teen, attempts the shooting and is killed by the crowd
Schirru tried by special fascist tribunal in 1931 and executed by firing squad
Sbardellotto's arrest, torture and execution close the run of attempts

notes: Re-published crossover from Cool People Who Did Cool Stuff (two parts in one file); hero chosen over crossover per the precedence rule and the 'cool people' cue. Primary is a group of assassins, so no single lifetime applies. Covered span starts with Bresci (1900, 1898 riots) and ends with partisan activity in 1945; Tomasini's 1968 activism is a brief coda. Terrorism vs fascism-far-right as primary is a judgment call.
